patterns.name: Iterative CSS Grid Layout Refinement Based on Visual Feedback
patterns.description: When user provides sequential screenshot feedback for layout issues, apply incremental CSS Grid adjustments with validation cycles rather than complete rewrites. Each iteration builds on previous changes to converge on desired layout behavior.
patterns.context: UI layout requirements clarified through visual feedback (screenshots with annotations). Initial implementation may not capture all requirements until user sees actual rendering behavior.

steps: Step 1: Create safety checkpoint commit before first change
Step 2: Implement initial interpretation of requirements
Step 3: Validate with clean build (0 errors, 0 warnings)
Step 4: Commit initial implementation with descriptive message
Step 5: Document changes in work log for traceability
Step 6: If user provides corrective screenshot, analyze delta from current state
Step 7: Apply targeted CSS adjustments (don't rewrite, refine)
Step 8: Validate again with clean build
Step 9: Commit refinement with clear distinction from previous attempt
Step 10: Update work log with refinement entry

equal_height_containers.problem: Grid items with different heights when using align-items:start
equal_height_containers.solution: Use align-items:stretch with height:100% on child containers

auto_expanding_grid.problem: Fixed height grid prevents content expansion
auto_expanding_grid.solution: Use height:auto on grid container, let content drive height

internal_scrolling.solution: Apply overflow:hidden to container, overflow-y:auto to internal flex child with min-height:0
internal_scrolling.code: .container { overflow: hidden; } .scrollable-child { overflow-y: auto; min-height: 0; flex: 1; }

examples.description: SessionCanvas layout refinement through 5 commits based on two screenshots

iterations.outcome: User provided second screenshot showing unequal heights

anti_patterns.description: Discarding all previous CSS and starting over after user feedback
anti_patterns.why_it_fails: Loses progress, increases risk of regression, wastes iteration cycles
anti_patterns.alternative: Analyze delta between current state and desired state, apply targeted fixes

anti_patterns.description: Treating initial screenshot requirements as comprehensive specification
anti_patterns.why_it_fails: Visual requirements often clarify through iteration as user sees behavior
anti_patterns.alternative: Expect refinement iterations, maintain clear commit history for rollback

debug_logging_strategy.placement: Document rationale for CSS decisions in code comments and Logger.LogInformation

patterns.name: CSS Grid Explicit Height Constraints
patterns.description: When using CSS Grid with percentage-based max-height, constraint is meaningless without explicit parent height. Use explicit pixel constraints instead to prevent expansion.
patterns.context: Grid containers where child containers have height: 100% causing vertical expansion, percentage-based max-height not working as expected

problem.description: Using max-height: 100% on grid child when parent has height: auto provides no constraint context

solution.description: Set explicit pixel constraints on min-height and max-height for both grid children to ensure matching heights

steps: Measure actual dimensions from user screenshot (e.g., 697px x 400px)
Apply matching explicit min/max constraints to both grid children
Remove percentage-based height: 100% that caused expansion
Verify grid layout respected with explicit constraints

success_indicators: Both containers maintain matching explicit height constraints
Content scrolls internally when exceeding max-height

patterns.name: Toast Notification Z-Index Layering
patterns.description: When toast notifications not visible despite library loaded, root cause is often missing CSS styling with proper z-index to render above other elements (especially debug panels).
patterns.context: Toastr notifications not appearing, rendering behind other elements, or invisible despite successful JSRuntime invocation

problem.description: Missing CSS styling causes toasts to render with default z-index behind other positioned elements
symptoms: Toast invocation succeeds but nothing visible
Toast appears behind debug panel or modal overlays
No visual feedback on notification calls

solution.description: Create shared stylesheet with high z-index (999999) and modern toast styling
solution.approach: 1) Extract toast styles from working example (session-transcript-styling.html), 2) Create wwwroot/css/noor-toastr.css with comprehensive styling, 3) Set z-index higher than debug panel (9999) and all other elements, 4) Add to all Razor views needing toast notifications

styling_requirements: High z-index ensures visibility above all content
Color-coded left borders for toast types (success: green, error: red, warning: amber, info: blue)

success_indicators: Toasts appear reliably on first invocation
Toasts render above all other elements including debug panel
Color-coded visual distinction between toast types

patterns.name: Overflow Visible for Badge Positioning
patterns.description: When absolutely positioned badges with transform: translate() extend beyond container bounds, change overflow-x: hidden to overflow: visible to prevent clipping.
patterns.context: Vote badges, notification indicators, or absolutely positioned elements being cut off at container edges

problem.description: overflow-x: hidden clips absolutely positioned elements extending beyond container
problem.broken_code: .container { overflow-x: hidden; position: relative; } .badge { position: absolute; transform: translate(50%, -50%); }

solution.description: Change to overflow: visible to allow badges to render outside container bounds

success_indicators: Badges fully visible even when positioned outside container
No visual clipping at container edges
